item.title: [6.8] ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Representative vision-language navigation (VLN) methods typically couple a vision-language model (VLM) brain with a learnable action head and fine-tune the VLM brain on navigation-domain data to predict geometric goals. However, such adaptation can substantially alter base VLM weights and degrade general visual capabilities. We introduce ZeroVLN, a slow-fast navigation framework that achieves...

WHY IT MATTERS

ZeroVLN presents a novel paradigm for Vision-Language Navigation by using a semantic tool-calling interface and closed-loop RL, avoiding costly SFT of the VLM brain and preserving general capabilities.
